q: What does sticky routing do to a two-backend fleet?
a: It pins every request to the first backend — the narration shows srv-a serving all 400 requests while srv-b serves zero.

q: Why does sticky fail at 120 RPS while least-connections passes?
a: One backend holds 100 RPS, so sticky's pinned load saturates it and drops begin; least-connections spreads roughly half each and stays green. Sticky wastes half the fleet.

q: What usually forces sticky routing in real systems?
a: Session state kept on the server — the balancer must pin each client to the machine holding its state. Prefer stateless servers with shared session storage.
